bikes.summary: A high-revving 250 whose strength is top-end and over-rev; most US testers still found the bottom end soft and needing the clutch, despite Honda's 2020 low-end changes. The Showa suspension was rated plush and easy to set up, though faster or heavier riders found the fork divey and the shock empty on G-outs. Testers reported a twitchy front or head shake in rough ground (one cause was a steering-head nut left loose from the factory) and an engine that runs hot when idling. Aftermarket full exhausts and a plug-in ECU were the usual low-end fixes.

points.statement: Bottom end feels soft and lazy; power comes in late and the clutch is needed to wake it up out of corners.
Pulls hard at high rpm and over-revs further than most rival 250Fs; it rewards being kept on the boil.
Showa suspension is plush and easy to set up for an average rider.
For fast or 170 lb-plus riders the fork dives under hard braking and the shock runs out of support at the end of the stroke on G-outs.
Front can feel twitchy, knife into corners or shake at speed in rough ground, especially for lighter riders; one cause found was a loose steering-head nut from the factory.
Runs hot when idling or in long high-rpm motos and can push coolant out of the overflow.
Aggressive map chosen for more torque out of corners; standard map also usable because it pulls longer in second and third.
Rear fender can break if used to lift the bike, engine-cover paint scratches early and the twin mufflers are costly to replace.

common_fixes.problem: Weak bottom end out of corners
common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket full exhaust system (slip-ons or silencer inserts lose most of the benefit)
common_fixes.result: Better bottom and low-mid pull and quicker second/third gear recovery, so a higher gear can be held; no top-end loss

common_fixes.fix: Plug-in aftermarket ECU
common_fixes.result: More low-end grunt and longer-pulling gears than any exhaust tested

common_fixes.fix: One tooth larger rear sprocket (13/49)
common_fixes.result: Third gear became usable in corners

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer fork compression and forks raised from 5 mm to about 3 mm in the clamps (back toward flush or 5 mm if it shakes or stands up)
common_fixes.result: Calmer front on braking and corner entry

common_fixes.fix: High-speed compression about 1/8 turn in and sag around 100-103 mm
common_fixes.result: Rear held up better on G-outs; 105 mm sag added stability but slowed turning

common_fixes.fix: Snug the steering-head nut
common_fixes.result: Front settled

sides: Most US tests found the low end soft and lethargic.
One Australian test of the 2020 found it pulled early with a strong midrange.

bikes.summary: The 2022 redesign swapped the old top-end character for much stronger bottom and midrange pull, but the engine falls off early on top and trails the class on peak power. Testers rate it among the best-turning 250s, yet most found the chassis rigid and touchy, with a twitchy front and head shake that needs setup work. The stock Showa fork was widely called too stiff and harsh while the shock felt soft, and both ends react to single-click changes. Common fixes are fork oil and valving changes, longer-offset clamps, a bigger rear tire and a tooth more on the rear sprocket.

points.statement: Much stronger bottom-to-mid pull than the 2020-2021 bike; it exits corners with little clutch.
Power falls off after the midrange and lacks over-rev, so a lower gear is often needed in corners.
Measured peak power sits at or near the bottom of the 250F class.
Third gear is short so riders often skip to fourth.
Frame feels rigid and touchy: twitchy front, mid-corner oversteer and head shake for lighter riders, with fore-aft balance hard to find.
Rated one of the best-cornering 250Fs and more forgiving leaned over than the 450.
Stock fork is firm and harsh late in the stroke for riders under about 170 lb while the shock is softer, leaving the bike unbalanced.
Very sensitive to single clicks, especially shock high-speed compression: stiffening it puts weight on the front and makes the fork harsher.
Stock 100/90-19 rear tire is too narrow for the engine's low-end and gives up grip at lean.
Build quality rated highly; the revised water pump stopped coolant loss and the nine-plate clutch survives abuse, though owners still name the clutch and stock chain as early wear items.
Measured among the lightest 250Fs after dropping the second muffler.
Seat foam breaks down in about 10-12 hours.
Upside-down air filter gets dirty quickly in dust; check it often.

common_fixes.fix: Lower fork oil level about 5 cc per leg and adjust compression; revalve for lighter riders
common_fixes.result: Less harshness deep in the stroke

common_fixes.fix: Slower shock low-speed compression and rebound instead of more high-speed compression
common_fixes.result: More hold-up and exit traction without loading the front

common_fixes.fix: Longer-offset clamps (23.5-24 mm vs stock 22 mm), plus correct springs, 105-108 mm sag and forks near flush; some added a steering damper
common_fixes.result: More stability on fast and rough tracks

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket linkage with a more linear rate
common_fixes.result: Plush start to the stroke that ramps up later

common_fixes.fix: 13/51 gearing
common_fixes.result: Third usable in corners

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket full exhaust
common_fixes.result: Kept the low end and added midrange, top and quicker recovery; second gear pulls longer

common_fixes.fix: 1.8 kg/cm2 high-pressure radiator cap
common_fixes.result: Holds coolant in hard use

common_fixes.fix: Firmer aftermarket foam
common_fixes.result: Lasts longer

sides: Most tests found the fork too stiff and harsh.
One 2022 shootout found it too soft with a light rear and added compression.
Several tests found it falls off early with a short top end.
One 2022 shootout found it linear and over-revving well.
Several tests called the frame rigid, harsh and nervous.
One tester found it forgiving leaned over and less rigid than the CRF450R.
One tester found the 2022 pump and louvers cured coolant loss.
Another recommends a higher-pressure cap because it overheats when worked hard.

bikes.generation: 2025-2026 (stiffer new frame, revised airbox, linkage and suspension)
bikes.summary: Testers broadly agree the 2025 frame fixed much of the earlier nervousness: the bike is more planted, precise and stable with less pitching, and still feels light. The engine is strong off the bottom but still trails the Austrian bikes and the Kawasaki on top, so most riders prefer the aggressive map. Suspension is plusher than before but soft for riders over about 175 lb or fast riders, and the stock 100/90 Pirelli rear is widely criticised. Common setup moves are lowering the forks toward flush, adding fork compression and stiffer springs for heavier riders.

points.statement: Strong off the bottom; easier to drive out of ruts and hold third gear than earlier bikes.
Mid-to-top pull and over-rev trail the Austrian 250s and the KX250; peak power measures roughly 3-4 hp down.
Aggressive map is the most common pick on the stock bike for its extra hit and pull.
More planted and precise with less pitching and front wiggle on entry; needs less effort to hold a line in braking bumps.
Can feel harsh in the forearms and busy under braking until fork height and clamp torque are adjusted.
Feels very light and easy to scrub and whip.
Fork is plusher over small bumps with a linear ramp; shock stays planted under power.
Both ends are soft for riders over about 175 lb or fast riders; the shock squats under acceleration.
Stock Pirelli 100/90-19 rear loses traction; testers want a 110 rear.
Revised front caliper gives a smoother, more linear feel.
Wider midsection grips well but tall riders' legs can catch the shrouds in deep ruts.

common_fixes.fix: Lower the forks from the stock height toward 2-3 mm or flush and run about 103-108 mm sag
common_fixes.result: Better cornering and stability

common_fixes.problem: Fork soft as the track roughens or on hard-pack
common_fixes.fix: Add 2-4 clicks of fork compression (and a couple of clicks of rebound on hard-pack)
common_fixes.result: Holds up better in braking bumps; cured instability on hard-pack

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer springs for riders over about 180 lb; fork revalve for heavier or fast intermediate riders
common_fixes.result: Better hold-up

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer shock low-speed compression (avoid stiffening high-speed, which made the front harsh)
common_fixes.result: More support and corner traction

common_fixes.fix: Lower triple-clamp pinch-bolt torque (check service manual minimums)
common_fixes.result: Less harshness and better front tire feel

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket full exhaust, run with the standard map
common_fixes.result: Felt about 2 hp stronger with better bottom, mid and over-rev

sides: Most testers prefer the aggressive map.
Another found the aggressive map runs out early and preferred standard.
Most testers say it lacks top-end punch.
One magazine's dyno runs looked better on top than expected, and a long-term tester said it did not feel slow on track.
One magazine saw no dyno gain from removing the filter cover and backfire screen.
A long-term test bike felt sharper response after removing the screen and enlarging the airbox hole, done together with an ECU remap.
One magazine liked stock gearing and changed nothing.
Other tests found first and second long and a gap to third that revs out quickly.
Most say it is strong off the bottom.
An Australian test wanted more torque out of turns in deep mud.

bikes.summary: Off-road testers like the RX engine: it pulls low, hits hard in the midrange and lets riders stay in a higher gear on tight trails. Its softer springs and valving are plush and good in rocks, but too soft for grand-prix pace without extra compression. Testers also mention a firm clutch pull, a wide tank and a wish for a sixth gear.

points.statement: Broad engine that pulls from low rpm, hits hard in the midrange and tolerates being a gear high while still revving.
Softer springs and valving are plush on track and trail and excellent in rocks.
Too soft for grand-prix speed: the fork wants a few clicks more compression and the shock is soft relative to the fork.
Clutch pull feels firm.
Oversized fuel tank is noticeable when putting a leg out.
Five-speed gearbox shared with the motocross bike; off-road testers want a sixth gear.

common_fixes.problem: Fork dives on big hits at speed
common_fixes.fix: Stiffen fork compression 1-2 clicks (or more) so it rides higher
common_fixes.result: Holds up better without losing much plushness

common_fixes.fix: Soften compression 2-3 clicks at both ends
common_fixes.result: Smoother in slow technical terrain

common_fixes.fix: Add sag and lower the forks in the clamps
common_fixes.result: More stability without giving up much cornering

bikes.summary: Little tester data so far. Off-road testers say the RX still pulls low and strong in the midrange, with the off-road map easing the hit, but it signs off on top earlier than some rivals. The stock front tire and the five-speed gearbox are the main complaints.

points.statement: Pulls low and strong in the midrange; the off-road map softens the transition into the main power, though the top end signs off earlier than some rivals.
Stock front tire gives poor grip.
Testers still want a sixth gear for off-road.
Fork is a touch soft relative to the shock on big hits.
Arm fatigue on long rides, blamed on the aluminium chassis.

common_fixes.fix: Two clicks more fork compression and 104-105 mm sag
common_fixes.result: Fork held higher in the stroke while staying plush

common_fixes.fix: Lower triple-clamp pinch-bolt torque and soften fork and shock high-speed compression
common_fixes.result: Less harshness through the bars

sides: One tester stiffened fork compression to hold it up.
Another softened high-speed compression over several rides for comfort.

bikes.summary: A powerful, light-feeling 450 with a well-liked rider triangle, but testers found the stiff chassis harsh on bumps and inconsistent from day to day. The clutch pull is heavy and the engagement narrow, and riders often calmed the delivery with ECU or exhaust changes. Fork dive under hard braking and an empty-feeling shock on G-outs were the main suspension notes.

points.statement: Stiff chassis feels harsh on bumps and twitchy at speed on rough tracks, and the bike feels different day to day.
Turns well and feels light; the lower 2020 battery position eases tip-in.
Rider triangle widely liked.
Heavy clutch pull and a narrow, on/off engagement.
2020 mapping is smoother off the bottom than 2019, but stock maps still deliver too much for anything but loam and roll on jerkily through corners.
Fork dives under hard braking at race pace; shock feels empty at the end of the stroke on G-outs.
Traction control helped most testers in slicker afternoon conditions.
Water in the handlebar map switch can stop the bike starting; engine oil darkens quickly.

common_fixes.fix: Lower swingarm-pivot and engine-hanger bolt torque and re-seat the engine (tilted up and back) before torquing
common_fixes.result: Softer square-edge feel, more rear traction, less vibration and easier initial lean

common_fixes.problem: Delivery and engine braking upset the chassis
common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket ECU with linear maps, or an aftermarket muffler with a smoother low end
common_fixes.result: Less engine braking and pitching; calmer chassis

common_fixes.fix: Longer aftermarket clutch arm or an auto-clutch style pack
common_fixes.result: Wider engagement, more clutch life and hook-up

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer fork compression and slower rebound; shock high-speed compression a quarter turn in at 105 mm sag
common_fixes.result: Calmer front and better G-out support

common_fixes.fix: Lower the forks in the clamps (flush or about 2 mm)
common_fixes.result: Calmer on fast tracks at some cost to turn-in

bikes.summary: Testers consistently praise this CRF450R's turn-in and rider triangle but call the chassis harsh on dry choppy tracks, nervous at speed and very sensitive to small setup changes. Early 2021 bikes ran rich and popped until Honda's dealer reflash; from 2023 the engine became more linear and torque-led. Stock suspension was the top complaint (soft in 2021, harsh or stagey later), and the most common fixes were revalving or stiffer springs, longer-offset clamps, an aftermarket ECU or exhaust and lower chassis bolt torques. A 1.8 radiator cap is a standard recommendation.

points.statement: Early 2021 bikes ran rich and dirty at low rpm, with popping in some maps, until Honda's dealer reflash.
From 2023 the engine is more linear and torque-led: precise throttle at low rpm, stronger low-mid and a less frantic top.
Standard map (map 1) is the usual choice; the aggressive map is sharper off the bottom but makes less peak power and can ping on hot days.
Sharp turn-in and precise in tight corners.
Harsh and tiring on dry, choppy tracks, loose at the rear on exits and prone to head shake at speed; happiest on smooth tracks.
Very sensitive to setup: a few mm of sag or 1 mm of fork height is felt, and a setting does not carry well from track to track.
At the stock 22 mm offset the front can feel heavy, knife into hooked ruts and oversteer in long rutted corners.
2023 frame and steel head stays made the rear calmer and more compliant in corners.
2021 suspension is soft and unbalanced for fast or heavier riders: the fork pitches and bottoms and the rear blows through in ruts.
2022-2024 fork is harsh in the mid or late stroke and the shock is stagey, harsh accelerating out of corners on baked, square-edged tracks.
Hydraulic clutch has a light, consistent pull and does not fade.
Hydraulic clutch engagement is narrow and on/off, and it is not bulletproof under hard racing.
Low-rpm vibration through the pegs and bars.
Slim bike with a rider triangle that suits most body sizes; the shift lever is short.
Radiators boil over quickly in hard use.
A 14-tooth countershaft sprocket can damage the clutch slave cylinder on 2021 bikes.
Upside-down air filter gets dirty quickly and is awkward to service; seat foam breaks down quickly; exhaust studs can back out.

common_fixes.fix: Honda dealer ECU reflash; map 3 until then
common_fixes.result: Cleaner low-rpm running; the fix became the 2022 standard map

common_fixes.problem: Engine braking and on/off feel upset the chassis
common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket ECU or a reflash of the stock ECU's maps 2 and 3
common_fixes.result: Less engine braking, cleaner low-rpm cornering, third gear lugs on stock gearing

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket exhaust (slip-on or full system)
common_fixes.result: Smoother low-rpm roll-on, less engine braking and pitching, more mid; one full system with an ECU flash measured about 4.7% more peak power

common_fixes.problem: Nervous at speed, knifing in ruts
common_fixes.fix: Longer-offset clamps (23.5-24 mm)
common_fixes.result: More stability and rut tracking, less vibration and harshness, turning kept

common_fixes.fix: Lower the forks from 5 mm to about 2.5 mm or flush
common_fixes.result: Calmer at speed without losing turn-in

common_fixes.fix: Lower chassis bolt torques slightly (axle, pivot, hangers) with thread locker
common_fixes.result: More compliance and traction; Honda responds to this more than other bikes

common_fixes.problem: Stock suspension soft for heavier or faster riders
common_fixes.fix: One spring rate stiffer at each end (fork about 5.1 N/mm, shock 56 N/mm)
common_fixes.result: Rides higher, more traction and track toughness, less oversteer

common_fixes.fix: Revalve fork and shock
common_fixes.result: More consistently plush fork and less loose feel at speed; owners name it the top improvement

common_fixes.problem: Shock harsh accelerating out of corners
common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket linkage with a flatter early rate and steeper late rate, plus lighter spring and matched valving
common_fixes.result: Corner-exit harshness roughly halved, better tracking

common_fixes.fix: Fit a 2023 Kawasaki KX master cylinder and flip the stock line
common_fixes.result: More progressive engagement

common_fixes.fix: Engine tilt procedure when torquing mounts, plus an aftermarket muffler
common_fixes.result: Reduced vibration

common_fixes.fix: 1.8 high-pressure radiator cap
common_fixes.result: Holds coolant in hard use

sides: One tester found it smoother and longer-pulling than 2020, easy to roll on.
Other tests found a low-rpm stumble and a steep surge around 7,000 rpm that was hard to manage.
Testers blamed an overly rigid aluminium frame.
Honda later said the old frame was among the softest and that flex caused the harshness; one tester also found the 2021 frame softer and straighter-tracking than 2020.
One tester rated it the best brake on a Japanese bike.
Another had it overheat within a few laps in a shootout.

bikes.generation: 2025-2026 (stiffer frame with 70% new parts, new linkage and suspension)
bikes.summary: Most testers say the 2025 frame transformed the CRF450R: more planted and stable at speed with less vibration, while keeping its sharp turn-in. The engine is the strongest of its year from low to mid and very usable, but tapers on top and measures a few hp behind the leaders. The plusher suspension suits lighter and slower riders; fast and heavier riders find it too soft and drop the forks, add compression or fit stiffer springs. A minority still report a harsh, kicking chassis on hard, edgy tracks.

points.statement: Very linear and usable with the strongest low-to-mid pull in its class; can pull third gear in corners.
Tapers off on top; peak power measures a few hp behind the class leaders, though it rides better than its dyno number.
Much better high-speed stability, less vibration and harsh slap-down, more neutral and less front-heavy in corners.
Accurate turn-in, strong on inside lines; it favours tight tracks over fast sweepers.
Coil fork is much plusher with no harsh spot.
Too soft for fast intermediates, pros and heavier riders: the fork dives under heavy braking and can bottom on big jumps, and the softer shock spring suits lighter riders.
Rider triangle rated best in class.
Shift lever is short and hard to get a boot under.
Brakes are not up to the European bikes' standard.
Three settings each for map, launch and traction control with flash codes and no phone app confuse riders.
Radiator boils over in hard use.
Stock 13/49 is close; some testers prefer 13/50.

common_fixes.problem: Fork soft on big jumps and under braking
common_fixes.fix: Lower forks to about flush-2.5 mm, add 2-3 clicks of fork compression and about half a turn more shock high-speed compression
common_fixes.result: Better balance and hold-up on big jumps

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer springs: about 5.1 N/mm fork and 54 N/mm shock over about 190 lb; owners around 180-200 lb report better feel with a stiffer shock spring
common_fixes.result: More support and better chassis feel

common_fixes.problem: Fast and pro riders want more support
common_fixes.fix: Send fork and shock out for firmer valving
common_fixes.result: Firmer setting suited to pace

common_fixes.problem: Harsh and unstable on fast hard-pack
common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket 23.5 mm split clamps
common_fixes.result: More flex, calmer chassis and better edge comfort; flat-corner exits less planted until the forks were raised

common_fixes.fix: Lower axle, clamp-pinch, pivot and shock-bolt torques slightly with thread locker
common_fixes.result: More compliance for one tester; owners report only partial improvement

common_fixes.fix: 1.8 high-pressure radiator cap in place of the stock 1.1
common_fixes.result: Stopped boil-over

sides: Most tests call the 2025-on chassis stable and largely bug-free.
One tester still found it harsh and unstable on fast hard-pack, some owners report a kicking rear on edgy tracks, and one 2026 shootout found it slightly front-heavy in rough high-speed sections.
One shootout called it well balanced since the 2025 frame stiffening.
Another found it slightly front-heavy in rough high-speed sections.

bikes.summary: Only one full test in the data. Its strong, throbbing low end defines the bike but is hard to manage in tight terrain, with a stall risk and heat build-up in clutch-heavy riding. Suspension is softer than the motocross bike yet resists bottoming well.

points.statement: Hits strong and throbbing down low and gets more frantic higher up; hard to control in tight terrain with a constant stall risk.
A little softer than the motocross bike but takes a big hit to bottom, and bottoming is well controlled.
Starts steaming with long first-gear or clutch-heavy riding on the stock radiator cap.
First gear is tall for tight trails.

bikes.summary: Testers call the RX a torque-first engine that is strong but tiring in tight trails. It feels less rigid and more planted than the motocross bike. Complaints include an on/off hydraulic clutch, a wide tank and traction control that helps on dry rocky ground but can bog on loose hills.

points.statement: Torque-first engine with strong pull; can be tiring in tight trails.
Feels less rigid and more planted than the CRF450R.
Hydraulic clutch pull is firm and engagement too on/off.
Oversized tank is felt when putting a leg out.
Traction control helps on flat, dry, rocky ground but can make the bike go flat on loose hills.
Softer and less supportive than the KX450X in a cross-country comparison.

common_fixes.fix: Add sag and lower the forks in the clamps
common_fixes.result: More stability without giving up much cornering

bikes.summary: Little tester data. The 2025 airbox softened the hit and cleaned up fueling with fewer stalls, and the smooth map with strong traction control makes it feel much milder for long or tight races. Suspension soaks up chatter but is soft for big motocross jumps.

points.statement: Torque-first delivery with a softer hit, cleaner fueling and fewer low-rpm stalls than before.
Smooth map with the strongest traction setting makes it feel like a 350, good for tight single-track; standard or aggressive suit loam and sand.
Settles further into the stroke and soaks up chatter, but is a bit soft for big motocross jumps.

common_fixes.fix: Add sag and lower the forks in the clamps
common_fixes.result: More stability without giving up much cornering

bikes.generation: 2020 (last year of the earlier engine, Showa coil fork)
bikes.summary: The 2020 KX250 revs freely with good mid-to-top pull and was one of the most stable 250s, but testers found it short on bottom end compared with the YZ250F and slightly down on low end versus 2019. An ECU remap was the main engine fix. Notes include a grabby rear brake, a tall bar and soft seat, a clutch that slips on hard exits and stock springs that suit a middleweight rider.

points.statement: Short on bottom-end grunt; needs a downshift more often than a YZ250F and feels slightly weaker down low than 2019.
More mid-to-top pull and rpm recovery than 2019; revs freely.
Straight-line stability and bump absorption among the best in its class.
Stock springs suit a middleweight: a 140 lb rider found them too stiff in braking bumps, while a 170 lb tester found the fork soft and pitchy on deceleration.
Rear sits low under acceleration and the end of the shock stroke is soft.
Front brake is strong, but the larger rear rotor is grabby and the pedal sits low with a long stroke.
Stock bar feels tall and wide and the soft seat centre lets the rider sink in.
Stock clutch slips on hard exits with good grip.
Wide gap from second to third makes skipping third common.
Stock map is conservative and the bike feels weighed down.

common_fixes.fix: Custom ECU map on the stock ECU
common_fixes.result: Stronger low and mid, freer revving, less engine braking and some exit torque back; quicker laps reported

common_fixes.fix: 110/90-19 rear tire
common_fixes.result: More bite and stability with no real downside

common_fixes.fix: Sag from 105 to about 103 mm and a quarter turn more high-speed compression
common_fixes.result: Better traction and front bite; rear held up on G-outs

common_fixes.fix: Softer fork and shock springs
common_fixes.result: Better braking-bump comfort; valving was close

common_fixes.fix: Fit the 2019 240 mm rear disc and hanger
common_fixes.result: Easier to modulate

common_fixes.fix: Lower-bend bar
common_fixes.result: Better front feel

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket clutch basket and pack
common_fixes.result: No slip and longer life

sides: Most describe white as aggressive and black as mellow.
One tester found white helped low-end recovery but fell off earlier on top, and another magazine called black the most aggressive low-end.

bikes.generation: 2021-2024 (big engine update, KX450-based frame, KYB coil fork)
bikes.summary: Testers describe a top-end engine: strong mid and top that revs very high, but weak initial response and low-end torque that hurt corner exits. It is stable in a straight line yet tends to push in flat turns because the engine sits far back in the 450 frame. The KYB fork was widely found stiff and harsh, especially for riders under about 165 lb. Long-term tests list many small quality problems (soft threads, fast-wearing chain rollers, cracking muffler tab), and the usual fixes are fork revalving or lighter springs, an aftermarket linkage, exhaust, ECU mapping and a bigger rear sprocket.

points.statement: Strong mid and top that revs very high; it rewards being ridden at high rpm.
Weak initial response and low-end torque hurt corner exits; it feels empty after the shift to third in deep dirt.
2023 engine has more midrange pull and a stronger top than 2022.
KYB fork is stiff and harsh in the midstroke, especially for riders under about 165 lb.
Pushes in flat or off-camber corners and can feel vague mid-corner; the engine sits far back in the frame and the fork rides high.
Stable in a straight line.
Soft threads strip easily (airbox bolt, fork-guard bolts, seat nuts).
Chain rollers, guides and sliders wear quickly; the front roller can come apart around 10 hours.
Coolant loss in sand and a weak stock radiator cap.
Muffler subframe tab cracks at the weld (worse with aftermarket exhaust) and a front engine-mount frame tab can crack after about 50 hours.
Steering-head bearings come with little grease and can fail within 20 hours.
A 2022 long-term bike broke clutch fibres and a main bearing in 75 hours; the 2023 reached 56 hours with no clutch-plate breakage.
Skinny levers cause blisters and the clutch feels on/off; grips are bonded to the throttle tube.
Stock 100/90 rear lacks bite.

common_fixes.fix: Revalve, lighter springs for light riders (about 4.7 N/mm) or remove fork oil
common_fixes.result: Most of the midstroke harshness removed; one revalve with springs cured about 85-90% of it

common_fixes.fix: Run less sag (about 100-103 mm), sit forward; avoid raising the forks
common_fixes.result: Weight onto the front and sharper turning

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket linkage, with sag reset to about 102-104 mm
common_fixes.result: Rear more planted and straighter in acceleration bumps, calmer on deceleration

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket exhaust and engine work (porting with ECU mapping)
common_fixes.result: More bottom and mid pull; some corners taken a gear higher

common_fixes.fix: One or two teeth larger rear sprocket (51-52T)
common_fixes.result: Better pull out of corners

common_fixes.fix: Custom map using the aggressive coupler's ignition with the mellow coupler's fuel, or Kawasaki's optional map
common_fixes.result: More midrange and longer pull, noticeable but not huge

common_fixes.fix: Cut the snout off the side panel to open the airbox
common_fixes.result: Sharper low-end response

common_fixes.fix: Auto-clutch style pack and a longer-ratio lever
common_fixes.result: Smoother engagement and longer life

common_fixes.fix: Grease them when new
common_fixes.result: Normal life

common_fixes.fix: 110/90-19 rear on the stock rim
common_fixes.result: More bite

sides: One tester found more low grunt than 2022.
A magazine found initial response detuned versus 2022, with weaker bottom snap but stronger mid and top.

bikes.summary: The 2025 KX250 split testers: faster riders found the engine heavier off the bottom with a narrow powerband, little recovery and less over-rev than 2024, while some novice and vet testers found it more usable. The new Showa fork is more compliant than the old KYB but soft for heavier or faster riders. The chassis turns more easily but feels stiffer and less stable at speed. Exhaust, airbox, ECU and gearing changes help response, though owners say it still feels slower-revving than the 2021-2024 bike.

points.statement: Narrow powerband that feels heavy off the bottom, with little recovery after a mistake and less over-rev than 2024; measured weaker than 2024 above about 6,500 rpm on one dyno.
Switch to the Showa fork made it far more compliant on corner entry.
Fork is soft, sits low and turns harsh for heavier or faster riders, and can feel busy at the top of the stroke on fast tracks.
Turns more easily with better front contact than 2024.
Chassis feels stiffer, twitchy and slightly less stable at speed, deflects and gets nervous when chopping the throttle.
Heaviest 250F in one comparison.
Most vibration of the 250Fs despite a new balancer.
Rear brake is hard to modulate and locks easily.
Shifting is notchy under load.
Brittle plastics, a strip-prone airbox bolt, a seat T-plate that can fall out, a low-pressure radiator cap and a restrictive airbox with a hard-to-seat filter.
Maps can be changed through the phone app; Kawasaki's optional maps cut engine braking and add low-mid response but shorten the pull in second and third.

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket air filter kit and trimming or opening the airbox
common_fixes.result: Sharper response

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket full exhaust
common_fixes.result: Stronger mid-to-top pull, smoother over-rev and faster recovery; second held longer and third usable in corners; small low-end gain

common_fixes.fix: Stock-ECU reflash or mapped aftermarket ECU
common_fixes.result: Better response and second-third pull; owners say it still revs slower than the 2021-2024 bike

common_fixes.fix: 51-tooth rear sprocket
common_fixes.result: Better low-end pull

common_fixes.fix: Lower the forks to flush (or about 3 mm), run the rear wheel back and speed up rebound
common_fixes.result: More stable into corners and less oversteer

common_fixes.problem: Fork too soft for heavier or faster riders
common_fixes.fix: Revalve with stiffer springs; an aftermarket linkage needs a shock spring about 0.1 kg/mm stiffer
common_fixes.result: Plush top, firm controlled midstroke, predictable bottoming and a more planted rear

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket engine mounts
common_fixes.result: More flat-corner lean grip, planted off throttle, better slap-downs

common_fixes.fix: 1.8 kg/cm2 cap
common_fixes.result: Holds coolant

sides: Faster riders and two magazines found it heavier, narrower and weaker on top than 2024.
Other launch tests found more usable low-to-mid power and easier starts, and novice and vet riders tended to prefer it.

bikes.summary: Off-road testers found the KX250X engine clean and happiest revved, with a strong top but limited bottom-end torque for technical terrain. The small tank, the stock front tire, the bulky kickstand and some head shake at speed were the main complaints. ECU remapping and gearing changes were the common upgrades.

points.statement: Clean and stall-free down low but short of bottom-end torque for off-road; a remap still left low end lacking.
Strong top end that keeps pulling a long way before the limiter.
First gear so short it is rarely used, and fifth runs out quickly.
Small tank ran dry around 55 minutes into a one-hour race.
Stock front tire has weak traction and stiff sidewalls.
Some head shake at speed; testers wanted a steering stabilizer for fast sections.
Bulky kickstand sits against the left leg.
Heavier vet riders found it under-sprung.

common_fixes.fix: ECU remap (one tester also preferred the aggressive coupler)
common_fixes.result: More power everywhere, though low-end torque was still lacking

common_fixes.fix: Tried 14/48, which was too tall and hard on the clutch in rocks; settled on 14/50
common_fixes.result: Workable gearing for fast terrain

common_fixes.fix: Larger aftermarket tank
common_fixes.result: Full race distance

common_fixes.fix: Soften low-speed compression 2-3 clicks at both ends and speed up fork rebound 1-2 clicks at 105 mm sag
common_fixes.result: Smoother off-road

sides: Two tests found it short of low-end torque for off-road.
A 2022 test found a decent bottom with enough torque and a linear build.

bikes.summary: Only one first-impression test. The new engine puts more weight on low and midrange torque, which suits technical riding. The softer Showa suspension is plush in slow terrain but rides low and harsh on deceleration at speed.

points.statement: More low and midrange torque than the earlier high-revving engine; easier in technical terrain.
Plush in slow terrain but low and harsh on deceleration at speed.

common_fixes.problem: Fork low on deceleration at speed
common_fixes.fix: A few clicks more compression and one click faster rebound
common_fixes.result: Rode higher in the stroke and more balanced

bikes.generation: 2019-2023 (2019-generation engine and frame, Showa coil fork)
bikes.summary: Testers rate this KX450 chassis among the most stable and forgiving of the aluminium-frame 450s, and it lays into ruts easily, though it can feel long with a vague front. The engine is smooth and usable rather than the strongest, with a touchy hit right off idle. The Showa fork is too soft and divey, the rear brake is grabby, and soft threads and a crack-prone muffler tab are recurring niggles. Stiffer fork springs or a revalve, ECU mapping, a slip-on with the stock header and the KX250's smaller rear rotor were the usual fixes.

points.statement: Very stable and compliant; frame absorption is among the best in its class and makes setup less critical.
Lays into ruts easily with good rear bite and is easy into and through corners.
Can feel long and lazy with a vague front mid-corner and once in a rut.
Touchy right off idle (0-10% throttle), which can upset it mid-corner.
Smooth and very usable rather than the strongest; lacks the mid pull of its main rivals in deep dirt and measures down on power from mid rpm up.
Showa fork is too soft: it dives, pitches and bottoms on hills and big jumps, and adding compression only makes it harsh.
Shock wallows and is soft on slap-downs and G-outs, squatting on exits for heavier riders; the stock link is harsh early and soft deep in the stroke.
250 mm rear rotor is touchy and locks early.
2021 clutch slips less with wider engagement and more traction.
Soft threads strip (seat nuts, airbox bolt in the subframe).
Muffler mounting tab on the subframe cracks, especially with solid-mounted aftermarket exhausts.
Fork guards and number plates crack and the lower chain roller wears fast.
Skinny clutch and brake levers cause blisters and the clutch feels on/off.

common_fixes.fix: One step stiffer fork springs (about 5.1 N/mm)
common_fixes.result: Better balance and decel-bump comfort, less oversteer

common_fixes.fix: Revalve (owners say it is valved soft rather than undersprung); one owner raised fork oil volume
common_fixes.result: Hold-up on deceleration and bump absorption without harshness

common_fixes.fix: More shock high-speed compression (up to about two turns in)
common_fixes.result: Less wallow

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket linkage, usually with a stiffer shock spring
common_fixes.result: Plusher early, firmer deep, straighter in acceleration bumps and calmer under braking

common_fixes.fix: Fit the KX250's 240 mm rear disc and hanger
common_fixes.result: Easier to modulate

common_fixes.problem: Touchy low end, dip from mid to top
common_fixes.fix: Custom ECU map or reflash; mellow coupler for slick tracks
common_fixes.result: Smoother off idle, dip filled, steadier in corners; owners call a reflash the cheapest effective upgrade

common_fixes.problem: Snappy, hard-to-control hit with an aftermarket system
common_fixes.fix: Slip-on muffler with the stock longer header
common_fixes.result: Smoother, more controllable power and better corner speed

common_fixes.fix: Rubber-mount the muffler bracket with the stock grommet, or have the tab re-welded
common_fixes.result: Saves the subframe

sides: One tester found it smoothed the low end with no loss of mid-top pull.
A magazine found it gives up 1-2 hp from 6,000 to 11,500 rpm and is too smooth in deep dirt.

bikes.generation: 2024-2026 (new engine top end, frame, Showa suspension and bar electronics)
bikes.summary: Testers agree the stock 2024-on KX450 feels mild and lethargic, more like a big 250 or a 350, with a restrictive airbox (including a hidden rubber plug) and muffler. The new chassis turns in far more sharply but can oversteer and shake its head at speed until the forks are lowered and the wheelbase lengthened. The fork is soft and pitchy with too little initial support. The most common fixes are opening the airbox, an aftermarket ECU and exhaust, a 51-tooth rear sprocket and stiffer fork settings.

points.statement: Stock engine feels mild, lethargic and heavy in tight corners, soft off the bottom and short on punch for starts, hills and deep sand.
Smooth and linear with good mid-to-top pull once revving; best ridden like a big 250.
Intake and exhaust are restrictive: a hidden rubber plug blocks part of the airbox and the stock muffler is choked.
Much sharper turn-in than before, with front-wheel traction while staying stable.
Can oversteer and shake its head at speed, and feels top-heavy in flat turns.
Fork is soft and pitchy with too little initial support, so it rides in the midstroke, dives under braking, bottoms and feels harsh on deceleration; the shock overpowers it.
Second gear is long and third feels far away.
Vibration through the bars at low rpm and the pegs at high rpm.
Measured about 5 lb heavier than the 2023.
Phone-app tuning offers few parameters and small gains, and a custom map saved to the second slot is detuned by the ECU.
Traction control helps on hard-pack under loose dirt and on uphills but does little on a smooth, dry day.
Some bikes leak oil from the right side-case gasket under the cylinder.
Stock air filter can be mis-installed and collapse inward, risking dirt ingestion.
A few owners reported very-low-hour engine failures or worn clutch plates around 20 hours; others report no problems.
Header nuts are nearly inaccessible.
Shock is plush, possibly soft for pros, though another tester found it firm in the midstroke and needing more hold-up.

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket ECU with tuner mapping, usually with an exhaust and opened airbox
common_fixes.result: Much stronger off the bottom and third gear usable in corners; one dyno showed almost 4 hp more, and riders felt about 6-7 hp

common_fixes.fix: Remove the hidden airbox rubber plug and drill or open the side cover/airbox
common_fixes.result: Better throttle response and bottom-end pull

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket slip-on or full exhaust
common_fixes.result: More response and midrange; one dyno test showed about 3 hp more at 7,500 rpm

common_fixes.fix: 51-tooth rear sprocket
common_fixes.result: Third more usable in corners

common_fixes.problem: Oversteer and head shake at speed
common_fixes.fix: Lower the forks to flush, add a chain link and run the wheel back, add fork compression
common_fixes.result: More stability at speed

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer fork springs (one or both legs) or about 10 cc more oil per leg, plus more compression
common_fixes.result: Better hold-up and bottoming resistance

common_fixes.fix: Shop revalve
common_fixes.result: More braking-bump support with the same ground-following feel; better shock control on acceleration and landings

common_fixes.fix: Kawasaki's optional app maps
common_fixes.result: More low torque feel and second-third roll-on, longer third

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket engine mounts and head stays
common_fixes.result: Less vibration

sides: Several tests found good mid-to-top pull.
One magazine found it broad and easy but lacking top end and torque.
2024 tests reported oversteer and head shake at speed.
2026 shootouts called the chassis stable, even best in class, though setup-sensitive.
One magazine rated the front brake excellent.
A 2026 shootout found it weaker than the class.
Magazine testers call it one of the best single changes.
One tester found 13/51 hurt second-gear pull and went back to stock.
One magazine's slip-on test showed no meaningful low-end gain.
Other testers felt more low-end pull from slip-ons and full systems.
One tester liked a lowering link on the earlier KX450.
On 2024-2025 bikes a tuner advised keeping the stock link because a lowering link softens shock feel; forum riders had no consensus.

bikes.summary: Testers found the KX450X's softer off-road suspension too soft at speed and on big hits, and stiffened fork compression as a first step. The front can feel vague on lean, the rear brake fades in heat on tight trails and the kickstand gets in the way.

points.statement: Stock suspension is too soft at speed: the fork blows through on bigger hits and rides low, and the shock lacks hold-up.
Front feels vague on lean and can wash suddenly or push on corner entry; some head shake at speed.
Rear brake fades in heat on tight trails.
Kickstand hits when leaning and stock levers are skinny.

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer fork compression and higher oil level, or an off-road revalve
common_fixes.result: Firmer end of stroke and better hold-up

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket 22 mm offset clamps
common_fixes.result: More front traction, slightly more feedback on fast square edges

common_fixes.problem: Rear could drive better through square edges
common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket linkage at 102 mm sag
common_fixes.result: More traction

common_fixes.fix: Larger-volume rear brake piston
common_fixes.result: Holds more fluid and sheds heat

bikes.summary: Little tester data. In a cross-country comparison the KX450X felt stiffer with more hold-up than its rival: good on fast courses, harder work in tight rocks and roots. One test noted it ran hot on tight technical trails.

points.statement: Stiffer with more hold-up than its main rival; good on fast courses but harder work in tight rocks and roots.
Ran hot on tight technical trails.

common_fixes.fix: Rear wheel back about 12 mm with extra chain links, 51-tooth sprocket, forks 2 mm up
common_fixes.result: Calmer at speed

common_fixes.fix: A few clicks more fork compression
common_fixes.result: Better support at speed
